clue.text: A traveller may find it necessary to overtake on the left

definitions.text: A traveller may find it necessary

parts.note: to overtake another vehicle is to pass it
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A driving tip: you may need to pass other cars on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like road advice; the definition is the opening phrase, describing a document no traveller abroad can do without.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document required for international travel.

clue.text: Place money aright and it will grow

parts.note: to pop something somewhere is to place it
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money
split as a + right, giving A and R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Invest your cash wisely and it will multiply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aright' is read as two words, 'a right', giving A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A poplar is a tree, something that grows.

clue.text: A big gun in the Dover area blew up

parts.note: Dover is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a toff is a grand or important person, a big gun

explanation.surface: A piece of artillery on the Kent coast exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A big gun' suggests artillery but means an important person; Dover is a port on England's south-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a charge is to detonate it, so set off means exploded.

clue.text: Talk about the Spanish church dignitary

indicators.note: about says one word goes around the other here

parts.note: to prate is to talk idly
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Gossiping about a senior Spanish cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking cleric such as a bishop.

clue.text: A motoring organisation to English people

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A motoring club dedicated to serving the English public.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a people or ethnic group sharing descent.

clue.text: City doctor admitted by a servant

indicators.note: admitted by says the doctor is let inside the servant

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

explanation.surface: A housemaid lets the town physician in.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain.

clue.text: Totally without reason a retiring person is quite inflexible

annotationWithheld.why: Totally without reason a retiring person is quite inflexible (7): ADAMANT; reversing MAD + A gives ADAM, but no clue word accounts for the remaining ANT, so the clue as held looks garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Totally without reason a retiring person is quite inflexible

clue.text: Fantastic Oriental tale

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly altered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic story from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is an account or narration of events, a story.

clue.text: Want to remove locks?

definitions.meaning: want in the sense of hardship or poverty
read playfully as dis- plus tress, to take away someone's hair

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into DIS (undo) and TRESS (a lock of hair); the question mark marks the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress means poverty or hardship, and whimsically means de-hairing someone.

clue.text: Long-suffering head accepting nice break

indicators.note: accepting says the head takes the other letters inside

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: break tells us to smash the next word and reassemble its letters

explanation.surface: A tolerant boss agreeing to a pleasant holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a boss in the surface, but here it is an old word for the skull, and 'break' is a holiday that turns out to be the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is the capacity to put up with trouble calmly, long-suffering as a noun.

clue.text: High fliers below par

definitions.meaning: birds of prey that soar at height
in golf, scores two strokes under par on a hole

explanation.walkthrough: In golf an eagle is a hole completed in two strokes fewer than par.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are large soaring birds, and in golf two-under-par scores.

clue.text: Testing, testing!

parts.note: a test done a second time, as a court case heard again before a new jury

explanation.walkthrough: The microphone check suggests sound engineering; the repetition of 'testing' points to a hearing held again.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a second trial of a case already heard.

clue.text: Fight for a really strong light

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud or strong
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Battling for a very bright lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: FF is the musical marking fortissimo, very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or disturbance.

clue.text: When beasts grab some he's off!

indicators.note: grab says the beasts take hold of the other piece, putting it inside

parts.note: deer are wild beasts
a part is some of something

explanation.surface: A man flees at the moment wild animals seize a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A departer is someone who leaves, one who goes off.

clue.text: Haul fish up where there's shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to haul or pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Pulling a catch aboard in the calm of the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the side sheltered from the wind.

clue.text: All the ritual bores a client to bits

indicators.note: breaking something to bits means its letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A customer is bored to pieces by all the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrations are ceremonies and rites, the ritual of festive occasions.

clue.text: Beat hands down, though not in form

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a form is a class at school

explanation.surface: Winning easily even when off one's best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' as a school class, and 'not in form' pretends to mean out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To outclass is to be far superior to, to defeat easily.

clue.text: Putting away the remains in some irritation

indicators.note: in places the remains inside the irritation

parts.note: a sting is a sharp irritation
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Storing cremated remains with some annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stashing means hiding or storing away for later.

clue.text: Sizable capital assets not declared?

parts.note: untold means not spoken or declared
wealth is one's assets

explanation.surface: A big fortune hidden from the taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: Untold also means beyond counting, so the phrase means an enormous fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immeasurable riches, a huge amount of capital.

clue.text: A plate of game everyone sent back

parts.note: a game leg is a lame one

indicators.note: sent back means the word for everyone is written backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A dish of game that the whole table returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here is the adjective meaning lame, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamella is a thin layer or plate, as in gills or bone.

clue.text: Offering a suggestion about the queen's residences

definitions.note: a terrace is a row of houses, so the singular names several residences

indicators.note: about means one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a trace is a slight suggestion or hint
ER is the royal cipher for the queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Proposing a hint about where the monarch lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, a set of homes.

clue.text: Discover a lever needs adjustment

indicators.note: adjustment signals that the letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Finding a lever that wants fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to uncover or disclose, the old sense of discover.

clue.text: Seating firm getting little support

parts.note: set means firm or solid
a golf tee is a small peg supporting the ball

explanation.surface: A furniture company receives meagre backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a piece of seating furniture.

clue.text: Only after money to get expensive stuff

indicators.note: after says the word for only comes behind the money

parts.note: cash is money
mere means only or just

explanation.surface: Purely interested in money, seeking luxury goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, costly wool fabric.

clue.text: Lament of the first King George and the first lady

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
I is the Roman numeral one, as in George I
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A complaint about George I and his queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first King George' is George I, GR plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to mourn or lament.

clue.text: Not all of the peers may wear a sword

indicators.note: Not all of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Only some lords are entitled to carry a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'may wear a sword' as the definition; only 'sword' names the answer, with 'may wear a' as link.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword.

clue.text: May be taken daily about five with great enthusiasm

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the numeral
taken here means taken apart, so the letters of daily are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A medicine to be swallowed daily, around five doses, eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be taken' pulls DAILY apart into ADILY, which goes around V.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidly means eagerly, keenly.

clue.text: A family man returned by himself — rift unmistakable

indicators.note: returned means the word for the family man is read backwards

parts.note: pa is a father, a family man
himself refers back to the family man, another pa
a rent is a tear or rift

explanation.surface: A father came home alone, the split in the family obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by himself' supplies a second PA beside the reversed one.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plain to see, obvious.

clue.text: Momentous communication

definitions.meaning: a message or sign passed on

explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means outstanding; as a noun, a sign or message conveyed.

clue.text: A stirring call for military personnel

definitions.text: A stirring call for military personnel

parts.words: A stirring call for military personnel
parts.note: stirring as in waking: the bugle call that rouses soldiers in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' looks like rousing or inspiring, but means waking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the morning bugle call waking troops.
